what: On is the Swiss running shoe brand, known for the hollow rubber pods in its soles. It sells through its own stores and website and through specialist running retailers.
customers: Runners and, increasingly, people buying the shoes to wear every day, in Europe, North America and Asia.
moat: A distinctive sole design people recognise at a distance, and tight control of where the shoes are sold, which has kept the brand premium while it scaled.
risks: 20 times earnings and growing fast, so the price assumes the growth continues
Running brands have risen and fallen before, and the category is crowded
Manufacturing is concentrated in Vietnam and Indonesia, which exposes it to tariffs
opportunities: Revenue grew from $794M to $3.8B in four years, among the fastest growth in consumer goods
A 6.8% net margin with $490M of free cash flow
Analysts see about 42% upside, with 31 covering the stock, and most of its growth is still in North America
watch: Direct-to-consumer revenue growth and the gross margin, which shows brand strength.
